description: Parent upload 2.0 stability PRD for the WeChat mini program, bridge, and website upload task pipeline. The goal is to make parent question upload feel smooth and recoverable from image selection, manual box selection, crop export, optional voice upload, server task submission, recognition polling, wrongbook refresh, and PDF availability. Stability is the priority: no unexplained spinning, no lost uploads, no whole-batch failure when one item fails, and no silent website/worker failure that leaves parents confused.
nonGoals: Do not reintroduce AI box selection in this PRD.
Do not add new parent-facing product features unless they directly reduce upload failure, waiting, or recovery friction.
Do not require parents to keep the page open until AI recognition and PDF rebuild finish.
Do not depend on production secrets, production data mutation, or manual server access for local proof.
Do not redesign the full mini program visual system; keep UI changes scoped to upload stability and feedback.
globalRules: Read AGENTS.md and handoff.md before each story.
Read miniprogram/handoff.md before each story that touches the mini program, bridge, upload APIs, worker, or wrongbook flow.
Work on exactly one user story per iteration.
Use the smallest possible edit that satisfies the acceptance criteria.
Do not refactor unrelated code or rename files unless a story explicitly requires it.
Every completed story must include runnable proof through a temporary script.
A story can only be marked passes=true after its focused proof and the mini program upload stability proof baseline pass.
Commit each completed story separately after verification.
Keep parent-facing failures specific and recoverable: accepted, still processing, partially failed, retryable, failed, and ready must not collapse into one vague spinner.
Every accepted upload item must keep a durable task id or visible failed state before local draft data is cleared.
experienceTargets: Parents should never see a silent spinner for more than 3 seconds during upload, crop export, task submission, polling, or wrongbook refresh.
Network acceptance should finish quickly once the cropped image and optional audio are uploaded; AI recognition and PDF rebuild should continue asynchronously.
If recognition takes longer than the active polling window, the UI should clearly say the upload was accepted and continues in the background.
Closing or reopening the page must not make accepted upload tasks disappear from the parent experience.
One failed crop, upload, task status request, recognition result, or PDF refresh must not make successfully accepted items look lost.

userStories.title: Create a single mini program upload stability proof runner
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need one documented proof path for parent upload stability so Ralph iterations do not guess which mini program, bridge, and website upload tests matter.
acceptanceCriteria: Add scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.

The proof must run parent upload page model tests, parent wrongbook preview tests, parent-only mini program scope tests, parentApi tests, bridge parent upload tests, bridge build, website WeChat parent upload data/API tests, and git diff --check.
The proof must not depend on production data, production secrets, Redis, RQ, a running Flask server, or a real WeChat device.
The proof output must make it obvious which command failed.
Run the helper from a temporary proof script and paste the full output.
Do not change parent upload behavior in this story.
userStories.notes: Completed during mini program upload 2.0 PRD bootstrap so the active Ralph queue can start with behavior hardening.

userStories.title: Add explicit parent upload stage feedback
userStories.description: As a parent, I need the upload page to show exactly what is happening instead of leaving me staring at a spinner during crop export, audio upload, image upload, task submission, recognition polling, and wrongbook refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit parent-upload/index.js and its model helpers for every submit-time busy state.
Add or extend tests for user-visible stages: preparing crop, uploading audio, uploading image, task accepted, recognizing, background processing, ready, partial failure, and failed.
The page must expose stage text or state that can be asserted without relying on real network calls.
Buttons that can corrupt the current job must be disabled only while the relevant stage is active, then re-enabled on failure or completion.
No stage may leave the page in an indefinite generic loading state after an exception.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This story attacks the parent-visible 'turning/spinning' complaint first.

userStories.title: Make upload task polling resilient
userStories.description: As a parent, I need task polling to survive slow recognition, flaky status requests, and mixed task outcomes without making accepted uploads look failed or lost.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace any all-or-nothing polling behavior that lets one rejected task-status request collapse the whole batch.
Add tests for mixed ready/failed/pending tasks, one transient status-fetch failure, malformed task payloads, and polling max-attempt exhaustion.
When polling max attempts are exhausted with pending tasks, the UI must communicate that uploads were accepted and are still processing in the background.
Task ids must remain available for later refresh or recovery after pending/polling timeout states.
A failed recognition item must be reported per item or in a partial-failure summary without hiding successful items.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Current polling window is short compared with real OCR/transcription/PDF latency.

userStories.title: Persist accepted upload tasks for page recovery
userStories.description: As a parent, I need accepted uploads to stay visible if I leave the page, WeChat reloads, the phone sleeps, or the network drops after submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Persist accepted upload task ids with enough child/image metadata to resume status checks safely.
Add tests for reopening the upload page with pending tasks and for clearing only tasks that reach terminal ready/failed states.
Do not re-upload a cropped image simply because a task is still pending.
If local storage is unavailable or corrupted, the page must degrade to a visible recoverable message instead of crashing.
The persistence key must be scoped so different parent/child contexts do not overwrite each other.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This keeps background processing from feeling like lost work.

userStories.title: Smooth manual crop and box interaction
userStories.description: As a parent, I need selecting, moving, resizing, rotating, and exporting question boxes to feel responsive and predictable on real phone photos.
acceptanceCriteria: Add focused tests for large portrait images, large landscape images, rotated images, tiny single-question boxes, switching current images, deleting the selected box, and exporting multiple boxes.
Crop export failures must be shown per item without clearing the whole draft.
The current selected image and selected box must remain stable after rotate, export failure, and delete operations.
The UI must not allow conflicting gestures or submit actions while a crop export is actively running.
Existing 1280 x 1792 / quality 0.82 export limits must remain protected unless evidence supports a safer change.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Keep manual box mode; do not bring back AI box selection.

userStories.title: Reduce upload timeout and retry frustration
userStories.description: As a parent on an unstable mobile network, I need transient audio/image upload failures to be retryable and understandable instead of waiting for a long opaque timeout.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit parentApi upload and request timeouts for audio upload, image upload, task submit, and task status fetch.
Add tests for timeout, 413 payload-too-large, transient 5xx, network fail, and user retry behavior.
Retryable failures must keep the original draft and show a retry path.
Non-retryable failures such as oversized payload after compression must produce a specific parent-friendly message.
Long server recognition must not be handled by keeping wx.uploadFile open for minutes.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: The old 180 second submit timeout should not be the parent experience.

userStories.title: Harden bridge upload proxy error mapping
userStories.description: As a parent, I need bridge failures and website failures to be mapped into clear retryable or final states, not vague upload failure messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend bridge parent upload tests for website 202 task acceptance, website 400 validation failure, website 413 payload too large, website 502 retryable enqueue failure, website timeout, and malformed website response.
Bridge responses must preserve website task ids and retryable flags when available.
Bridge must not turn a website accepted task into a local failure because optional fields are missing.
Parent-facing mini program helpers must receive enough structured error data to show specific messages.
Do not change unrelated bridge routes.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This story focuses on the miniprogram/backend bridge layer.

userStories.title: Harden website upload task API and enqueue semantics
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the website upload API to make task acceptance, enqueue failure, task status, and retryability unambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend website tests for /api/wechat/wrong-questions task creation, enqueue failure, unauthorized task status access, stale/pending task status, ready task status, failed task status, and retryable fields.
If RQ enqueue fails, the API must leave an inspectable failed task state and return a retryable error without pretending the upload was accepted.
Task status payloads must include enough stable fields for the mini program to distinguish pending, processing, ready, failed, and missing record states.
The API must not require child reason text or voice audio for image-only upload.
Do not require a live Redis/RQ process in local tests; mock queue behavior where needed.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This protects the website side from becoming the hidden source of spinning.

userStories.title: Preserve submitted images through recognition and PDF failures
userStories.description: As a parent and teacher, I need a submitted question image to remain visible even if transcription, OCR, reason classification, or PDF rebuild fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend worker/API/data tests so AI recognition failure still creates or preserves a teacher-visible wrong question record with the original image.
PDF rebuild failure must not erase the accepted upload task or original submitted image.
Task failure payloads must expose a concise reason for the parent while keeping enough detail for maintainers.
Successful items in the same batch must still reach ready even if another item fails.
No production data repair script may be required for the local proof.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Parents can tolerate slow AI better than losing the submitted question.

userStories.title: Refresh parent wrongbook and PDF state after upload
userStories.description: As a parent, I need to know where my uploaded question went, and the wrongbook/PDF entry points must be honest when recognition or PDF rebuild is still in progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Add tests for parent wrongbook refresh after ready tasks, failed tasks, and background-processing tasks.
After upload acceptance, the parent must have a clear path to check progress or open the child's wrongbook without losing status.
PDF actions must handle not-yet-ready, missing pdf_url, download failure, and openDocument failure with visible recovery messages.
Wrongbook cards must not imply AI recognition succeeded before ready status or recognized record data exists.
Do not add teacher-only controls to the parent mini program pages.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This closes the loop between upload and the parent-visible wrongbook/PDF experience.

userStories.title: Add production upload pipeline smoke runbook
userStories.description: As an operator, I need a repeatable production smoke checklist for Flask, bridge, Redis, RQ worker, upload size limits, task queue, and PDF output before asking parents to try the upload flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or update a concise runbook under docs/ or scripts/ralph/ that covers PM2 services, Redis health, RQ worker health, bridge health, Flask health, upload size limits, sample task status, and wrongbook/PDF refresh checks.
Include exact commands that are read-only unless explicitly labeled otherwise.
Include the expected healthy result for each check.
The runbook must call out what to do if tasks stay pending, enqueue fails, uploads hit 413, or PDF refresh fails.
Add a lightweight local proof that validates the runbook references existing scripts/routes where practical.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This is for release readiness; do not mutate production during automated proof.

userStories.title: Add parent upload 2.0 acceptance guardrail
userStories.description: As the product owner, I need a final guardrail that proves the parent upload 2.0 stability contract stays intact across mini program, bridge, website API, worker, and wrongbook/PDF behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a final local acceptance proof or checklist script that exercises the documented happy path and the main failure paths with mocks or deterministic fixtures.

The acceptance proof must cover select image, create box, optional voice/text reason, crop/export, submit, task accepted, polling ready, polling failed, polling still pending, wrongbook refresh, and PDF not-ready behavior.
The proof must verify no active code path refers to AI box selection as a current capability.
The proof must verify every user story in this PRD is passes=true before reporting complete.
Update progress.txt with the final 2.0 status and remaining manual smoke requirements.
Run the mini program upload stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This story is the final Ralph completion gate for the parent upload 2.0 stability PRD.
